claim: BatDetect2 jointly detects and classifies individual bat echolocation calls and reports a time-frequency bounding box and predicted class for each call.
scope: bat call detector proposals, event localisation, and tool validation
limitations: Model outputs are predictions rather than ground truth; the bundled classifier is trained for UK bat species and its taxonomy is not directly transferable to Australian species labels.
source_citation: Mac Aodha, O. et al. (2022). Towards a General Approach for Bat Echolocation Detection and Classification. bioRxiv. https://doi.org/10.1101/2022.12.14.520490

provenance.source_type: primary preprint and official software record

claim: BatDetect2 outputs should be validated on known local data before they are used for biodiversity assessment because deployment audio may differ from the model's evaluation data.
scope: detector uncertainty, distribution shift, proposal validation, and human review
limitations: This is operational guidance from the official BatDetect2 software record, not a calibrated uncertainty estimate for a particular recording.
source_citation: Mac Aodha, O. et al. BatDetect2 official repository and documentation. https://github.com/macaodha/batdetect2

claim: iBatsID was designed to provide objective acoustic species identification that is consistent, repeatable through time, and comparable across European monitoring programmes.
scope: standardised bat acoustic identification and reproducible tool use
limitations: The claim concerns European species classification from call parameters; it does not validate event boxes or Australian taxonomy.
source_citation: Walters, C. L. et al. (2012). A continental-scale tool for acoustic identification of European bats. Journal of Applied Ecology, 49, 1064-1074. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1365-2664.2012.02182.x

claim: Acoustic identification performance depends on the quality and representativeness of the reference call data used to develop and test the classifier.
scope: reference libraries, classifier uncertainty, and limits on generalisation
limitations: Reference-library adequacy is species- and region-dependent; this evidence does not supply a decision rule for individual event geometry.
source_citation: Walters, C. L. et al. (2012). A continental-scale tool for acoustic identification of European bats. Journal of Applied Ecology, 49, 1064-1074. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1365-2664.2012.02182.x

claim: PCEN replaces static log or root compression with per-channel automatic-gain-control-based dynamic compression to improve robustness to loudness variation.
scope: audio preprocessing, signal contrast, and representation selection
limitations: The reported experiments concern keyword spotting, not bat-call bounding-box annotation; improved recognition cannot be assumed to preserve localisation geometry.
source_citation: Wang, Y., Getreuer, P., Hughes, T., Lyon, R. F., and Saurous, R. A. (2017). Trainable Frontend for Robust and Far-Field Keyword Spotting. ICASSP. arXiv:1607.05666.

provenance.source_type: peer-reviewed conference paper and author manuscript

claim: The main PCEN gain-control and smoothing parameter choices depend on the loudness distribution of the data, and trainable PCEN learns such parameters jointly with the task model.
scope: preprocessing parameter calibration and representation uncertainty
limitations: Parameters learned for speech keyword spotting do not establish suitable settings for ultrasonic bat recordings or visual annotation by a VLM.
source_citation: Wang, Y., Getreuer, P., Hughes, T., Lyon, R. F., and Saurous, R. A. (2017). Trainable Frontend for Robust and Far-Field Keyword Spotting. ICASSP. arXiv:1607.05666.

provenance.source_type: peer-reviewed conference paper and author manuscript
